attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated as his belief and called an inevitability.

semantics.note: 'I believe' is backed by 'will collapse' and 'This is an inevitability', so this is a firm forecast, not hedged. The proposition keeps 'vast majority' and the payment trigger. It has no deadline.

contract.note: The plain reading of collapse (default, insolvency, closure or abandonment caused by weak paying demand) and of 'vast majority' (well over half) is ordinary and fair. Counting projects and the timing of the payment test are the evaluator's choices, which the contract flags. The four-year reference is correctly not treated as a deadline.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's own Q2 2026 release about one operator. It is not independent and says nothing about failure rates across the whole population.
Published 26 Oct 2026, before the cutoff. It reports forecasts (Gartner, Musk) about neoclouds, not completed failures.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no qualifying collapses across the population and no completed outcomes that would rule out a vast-majority failure. The CoreWeave figures and the third-party forecasts are context only. The forecast cannot be settled yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sidenote in his own article.

semantics.note: The causal claim (subsidised subscriptions inflate demand) and the price disparity are kept. The proposition slightly underplays 'effective subsidization', but the meaning holds.

contract.note: Reading 'worth' at API prices and 'tens of thousands' as at least $20k a month is ordinary. The contract rightly separates API-equivalent value from real cost, and requires both services and July 2026 conditions.

evidence.note: July 2025 report of one Anthropic power user. It is from a different period, has no valuation method and covers no ChatGPT usage.
2025 Claude rate limits. Different period, and the limits changed later.
Anthropic's May 2026 disclosure that it raised limits. It gives no monthly API-equivalent usage and no measure of the effect on demand.

reviews.rationale: None of the evidence covers July 2026 usage on either service, and nothing covers ChatGPT. Nothing isolates the effect of subscription pricing on compute demand. The Anthropic items are from other periods or are company disclosures, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article.

semantics.note: 'All it takes' asserts that the defaults would be enough, so 'will' is right. The antecedent of ten or fifteen defaults is kept. The subprime comparison is framing.

contract.note: Reading 'panic' as broad repricing or a financing freeze is ordinary. Counting distinct defaulted loan facilities is reasonable. The open window and lag are flagged.

evidence.note: A secondary tracker dated 17 Oct 2026. It shows no public foreclosure of a GPU-backed loan and no qualifying cluster of defaults. It establishes neither the antecedent nor the market response.

reviews.rationale: Conditional forecast whose antecedent is unknown: the packet records no ten to fifteen qualifying defaults. Under the policy a conditional with an unknown antecedent is not scored, and there is no deadline, so it remains unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own article.

semantics.note: The text is quoted faithfully. But 'for many of the same reasons' is a causal claim, not a scope condition, and the contract scores it on the causal axis. So causal fits better than observation.

contract.note: The plain reading (speculative investment substantially exceeds paying demand, with shared mechanisms such as capital flows, chasing yield and mispriced risk) is fair. Using Q1 2026 as the observation period is the evaluator's substitution, and the contract flags it.

evidence.note: CBRE vacancy data for Q1 2026, published before the cutoff. It covers broad colocation markets, not AI compute demand, so it cannot settle the claim either way.
ECB May 2026 assessment of AI financing risk. It is about risk and does not establish excess or shared causes.
Bernanke's 2009 account of the role of capital inflows in the financial crisis. It is evidence about the historical episode only.

reviews.rationale: No item measures speculative financed AI capacity against paying demand. Nothing shows that crisis-era mechanisms caused the AI investment. The vacancy data, the ECB risk warnings and the historical speech are context only, so the claim is unresolved.
